evals.name: hash-table-hot-loop
evals.prompt: Our Rust simulation step is slow. The profile shows 60% of time in HashMap<u64, Entity> lookups inside update_positions(), which reads only position and velocity for every entity each tick. Entity IDs are assigned by us at spawn time. Make it faster.
evals.expected_output: Records a baseline, replaces the hot-path HashMap with dense IDs indexing contiguous storage, considers structure of arrays for the position/velocity fields read every tick, states the invariant for removed or reused IDs, and reports before/after numbers from the same harness.

assertions.text: Proposes dense integer IDs and flat array indexing instead of the hash lookup on the hot path
Considers structure of arrays or a hot/cold split because the loop reads only two fields
States how stale or reused IDs are prevented (generations, append-only, or equivalent)
Measures before and after with the same workload rather than asserting a speedup

evals.name: cache-requested-as-fix
evals.prompt: resolveModulePath() in our bundler is slow on big monorepos. Just wrap it in an LRU cache so the benchmark goes green.
evals.expected_output: Does not silently add the cache. Investigates why resolution is slow (repeated string hashing, filesystem walks, pointer-heavy lookup tables), proposes a redesign of the base path, and presents a cache only as an explicit tradeoff the user can opt in to.

assertions.text: Asks or measures why the uncached path is slow before choosing a fix
Proposes a redesign of the underlying lookup instead of defaulting to a cache
If a cache is still offered, it is presented as an explicit user decision with its tradeoff

evals.name: delete-all-caches-literal
evals.prompt: Jarred says caching is cope for a slow design, so delete every cache in our payments service: the in-memory price memo, the idempotency-key store, and the cache in front of the paid FX-rate API.
evals.expected_output: Classifies each cache. The price memo is a performance memo and a removal candidate once a measured redesign makes it unnecessary. The idempotency-key store is correctness-bearing and stays. The FX-rate cache protects cost and rate limits and stays. Both kept caches are reported as decisions for the user.

assertions.text: Does not remove the idempotency-key store
Does not remove the cache in front of the paid external API without an explicit user decision
Treats the price memo as removable only after a redesign is measured to be at least as fast

evals.name: correctness-bug-first
evals.prompt: The tokenizer drops the last token when input has no trailing newline, and it's also kind of slow. Rewrite it to be data-oriented.
evals.expected_output: Fixes the dropped-token bug first with a regression test, then applies data-oriented changes only if a measurement shows the tokenizer is a meaningful cost, preserving output semantics.

assertions.text: Fixes and tests the correctness bug before any performance rewrite
Does not change tokenizer output semantics during the optimisation

evals.name: bottleneck-elsewhere
evals.prompt: The orders page takes 4 seconds. Can we convert the Order objects to a structure of arrays to speed it up? The trace shows 3.6s spent in 400 sequential SQL queries.
evals.expected_output: Points out that the measured bottleneck is the N+1 query pattern, not memory layout, recommends batching or joining the queries, and does not restructure Order into SoA.

assertions.text: Identifies the database queries as the measured bottleneck
Does not convert Order to structure of arrays

evals.name: microbenchmark-theater
evals.prompt: I switched our parser's node list to SoA and a 10-element microbenchmark is 3x faster. Ship it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a 10-element benchmark fits in cache regardless of layout and may not reflect the real workload, asks for or runs a representative workload, and recommends shipping only if it wins there without semantic changes.

assertions.text: Flags the tiny benchmark as unrepresentative
Requires a representative end-to-end measurement before recommending the change

evals.name: pack-bits-into-index
evals.prompt: Every AST lookup in our Zig compiler first checks the node's kind. Nodes are referenced by u32 index. Can we pack the kind into the index?
evals.expected_output: Sizes the bit split against the maximum node count, centralises masks and shifts behind named functions, adds a compile-time or construction-time capacity check, and measures the change.

assertions.text: Chooses the bit split from capacity requirements and enforces it with an assertion or checked constructor
Keeps masks and shifts behind named helpers rather than scattering bit arithmetic
Splits the index into a kind field and an index field with a stated capacity

evals.name: small-hot-path-edit-proportional
evals.prompt: Add a `visited` flag check to the inner loop of our graph traversal in traverse.go. It runs per edge.
evals.expected_output: Makes the small edit and briefly considers whether the flag belongs in a dense bitset or parallel array next to the node index rather than on a pointer-heavy struct. Mentions only decisions that change the implementation; does not launch a full redesign or report.

assertions.text: Keeps the response proportional to a small edit, without an unrequested full redesign
Considers data layout for the per-edge flag only where it changes the implementation

evals.name: no-performance-goal
evals.prompt: Add a settings page to our admin dashboard that lets admins rename their workspace.
evals.expected_output: Does not apply data-oriented performance guidance; builds the feature with normal maintainable code.

assertions.text: Does not introduce flat arrays, bit packing, SoA, or cache removal into ordinary feature work
